en: The Jātaka: The Fifth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Arising of Beauty.
“By means of beauty, lineage, strength, and prowess;”
“Subāhu, you say, ‘There is no one better than me,’ yet you speak thus, Sudāṭha.
[Yet you are surpassed] in beauty, stature, and birth.”
And because of his departure with the army,
you say that Subāhu was better than Sudāṭha for me.
If you speak thus to me while I am dwelling in this way,
Subāhu, my friend, you have spoken ill;
I shall no longer associate with you.
I delight in dwelling with one who would believe the words of others exactly as they are.
One quickly breaks with a friend and engenders much enmity;
he is not a friend who is always heedful.
One who fears division and perceives only the vulnerability [of others],
and upon whom one rests as if on one's own breast like a son—
he indeed is a friend who cannot be alienated by others.
The Vaṇṇāroha Jātaka is the first.
